title: 3 Stocks to Buy During This Earnings-Driven Market Selloff
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; collaboration with The Motley Fool (Neil); note: captions garbled in places
summary: Couch Investor hosts Motley Fool's Neil for an earnings-season watchlist video covering three stocks amid a volatile, earnings-driven selloff. Neil's first pick is SoFi (SOFI), a ~$20-22B fintech down ~37% this year before a triple-beat Q3: 2026 revenue guidance raised again to +40%, with 2027 guidance already given at +27% revenue, ~35% adjusted EBITDA margins and 90c EPS, putting it near 20x next-year earnings, which Neil calls very cheap. Lending is strong and financial services are re-accelerating, though the technology platform still lags. Couch Investor's own pick is Amazon (AMZN): AWS grew 40% year over year to $46B in Q3, its fastest in nearly five years and sixth straight quarter of acceleration, a $184B annualised run rate supplying ~63% of operating profit. Negative free cash flow of -$42.4B and debt up from $66B to $173B are framed as the cost of funding AI growth, with 2026 capex heading toward ~$220B and AWS growth above 40% expected in 2027 and 2028. Neil's third pick is Nvidia (NVDA), a ~$5T company at ~17.5x forward earnings with revenue up 90.6% this fiscal year and guided +70%+ next, ~$190B of free cash flow rising toward ~$450B in two years, sovereign AI tripled to ~$30B, and CUDA lock-in. Risks named are growth decelerating in about two years and custom-chip competition from Broadcom, Marvell, Google TPUs and AMD. Calls: SOFI BUY, AMZN BUY, NVDA BUY — all reiterated, no flips.

calls.base_case: 2027 revenue +27%, adjusted EBITDA margins ~35%, EPS 90c on management's own rate-hike assumptions.

calls.bear_case: Rates stay elevated or rise again (management assumes two more hikes in 2026, two in 2027); lending and tech-platform growth slow.
